text:
# Authentication

All API requests must be authenticated and sent over HTTPS. Requests over plain HTTP are rejected.
heading: Authentication

text:
## API keys

API keys are the primary authentication method. Send the key in the `Authorization` header using the Bearer scheme: `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>`. Keys are created in the dashboard and are shown only once at creation. Each account can hold up to 10 active keys. Keys should be rotated at least every 90 days.
heading: API keys

text:
## OAuth 2.0

For server-to-server integrations, the API supports the OAuth 2.0 client credentials grant. Access tokens are obtained from the `/oauth/token` endpoint and expire after 1 hour. Refresh tokens are not issued for the client credentials grant; request a new access token instead.
heading: OAuth 2.0

text:
## Mutual TLS

Mutual TLS (mTLS) is available as an additional authentication layer on the Enterprise plan only.
heading: Mutual TLS

text:
## Unsupported methods

HTTP Basic authentication and passing API keys as query string parameters are not supported.
heading: Unsupported methods

# Data Retention and Deletion
heading: Data Retention and Deletion

text:
## What we retain

Customer records you store through the API are retained for as long as your account is active. API request logs are retained for 90 days. Aggregated usage metrics are retained for 13 months for billing purposes.
heading: What we retain

text:
## Deletion requests

You can delete a customer record with `DELETE /v1/customers/{id}`. On Free and Pro plans, the record is removed from the live database immediately but is fully purged from all systems, including backups, within 30 days.

Immediate permanent deletion, including removal from backups, is only available on the Enterprise plan by adding the `purge=true` query parameter. Purge requests on other plans are rejected with HTTP 403.
heading: Deletion requests

text:
## Account closure

When an account is closed, all customer data is deleted within 30 days. Backups are rotated every 35 days, so residual copies in backups are gone no later than 35 days after closure.
heading: Account closure

text:
# Pricing

Nimbus API offers three plans. All prices are in USD and billed monthly.
heading: Pricing

text:
## Free plan

The Free plan costs $0 per month and is available to any individual or company, including startups. It includes 10,000 API requests per month and a rate limit of 60 requests per minute. Webhooks are limited to 3 endpoints. No credit card is required to sign up.

There is no separate plan or discount program specifically for startups. Startups that outgrow the Free plan move to the Pro plan like any other customer.
heading: Free plan

text:
## Pro plan

The Pro plan costs $49 per month. It includes 500,000 API requests per month and a rate limit of 600 requests per minute. Requests above the monthly quota are billed as overage at $0.50 per 1,000 requests. Pro accounts can configure up to 25 webhook endpoints.
heading: Pro plan

text:
## Enterprise plan

Enterprise pricing is custom and negotiated annually with the sales team. Enterprise accounts get custom rate limits, unlimited webhook endpoints, mutual TLS authentication, and immediate data purge on request.
heading: Enterprise plan

text:
## Billing

Invoices are issued on the first day of each month. Downgrading from Pro to Free takes effect at the end of the current billing period. Unused requests do not roll over to the next month.
heading: Billing

text:
# API Rate Limits

Rate limits are applied per API key using a sliding one-minute window.
heading: API Rate Limits

text:
## Limits by plan

- Free: 60 requests per minute
- Pro: 600 requests per minute
- Enterprise: custom, set in the contract

Short bursts of up to 2x the per-minute limit are tolerated for at most 10 seconds.
heading: Limits by plan

text:
## Exceeding the rate limit

When a client exceeds its rate limit, the API rejects the request with HTTP status 429 Too Many Requests. The response includes a `Retry-After` header giving the number of seconds to wait before retrying. Rejected requests are not counted against the monthly quota.

Every response carries `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, and `X-RateLimit-Reset` headers so clients can throttle themselves before hitting the limit.

If a key keeps exceeding its limit continuously for more than 15 minutes, the key is temporarily blocked for 1 hour and the account owner is notified by email.
heading: Exceeding the rate limit

text:
## Recommended client behavior

Clients should retry 429 responses with exponential backoff, starting at the `Retry-After` value and doubling on each attempt, up to a maximum of 5 retries.
heading: Recommended client behavior

text:
# Webhooks

Webhooks notify your server when events happen in your Nimbus account, such as `job.completed`, `job.failed`, and `customer.deleted`.
heading: Webhooks

text:
## Signature verification

Every webhook request includes a `Nimbus-Signature` header containing an HMAC-SHA256 signature of the raw request body, computed with your endpoint's signing secret. Verify the signature before trusting the payload. Requests also carry a `Nimbus-Timestamp` header; reject any delivery whose timestamp is more than 5 minutes old to prevent replay attacks.
heading: Signature verification

text:
## Delivery and retries

Your endpoint must respond with a 2xx status code within 10 seconds. Any other response, or a timeout, counts as a failed delivery. Failed deliveries are retried up to 8 times with exponential backoff over a period of 24 hours. After the final retry fails, the event is marked as failed and the endpoint is disabled if it has failed every delivery for 3 consecutive days.
heading: Delivery and retries

text:
## Delivery logs

Webhook delivery logs, including request payloads, response codes, and timing, are retained for 30 days and can be viewed in the dashboard. Failed events can be replayed manually from the dashboard while their log entry still exists.
heading: Delivery logs
